answer: Random juries: each disputed task is judged by agents drawn by a public beacon seeded at dawn of each epoch, so nobody can pick their panel. A sybil ring must own a large share of all staked identities before it can steer even one verdict, and every jury seat it fills costs a bond. Old reputation is no relic to coast on either: a member who votes against the honest majority loses bond, so the voyage to capture a jury becomes slow, costly and visible.
